question: Does test risk turn upward because target fitting and sample-noise fitting occur at different spectral times?

data.noise: independent Gaussian per training row; clean test labels; same eps/noise samples reused across paired activation andscale

noise_risk_theory: Fit separate clean and epsilon heads on same fixed features; clean-test MSE = signal-bias + realized-noise-energy + cross-term. Expected variance over iid trainnoise uses exact spectral estimator, no fittedtime parameter.

predictions.claim: Noisy training MSE does not turn up while expected clean-test risk can turn up.
predictions.criterion: all64train curves monotone to tolerance1e-10; n32 ReLU noise1 expected risk has an interior minimum followed by increase>=.05 at16384 for>=3/4seeds

predictions.claim: The risk decomposition and conditional noise-variance prediction identify noise fitting rather than scalar nominal U as the source of the late increase.
predictions.criterion: risk decomposition error<1e-8; expected-noise-energy nondecreasing allconditions; at n32 ReLU mean late noise growth exceeds mean late signal-bias reduction after expected-riskminimum
predictions.scope: expected-risk minimum is descriptive, not deployment early-stoppingselection

predictions.claim: More samples reduce final expected noise-driven risk for ReLU under this matched target/width.
predictions.criterion: mean expected final risk n128<n32 atnoise1; reportallseeds/actualrisk
predictions.scope: new pointdraws; not same-population universal law

predictions.claim: Small-SiLU delays learning even signal and noisy nonlinear modes, so its optimum is not the same nominal U as ReLU.
predictions.criterion: n32noise1 median expected-riskminimum step small-SiLU>ReLU; finalnoisevariance small-SiLU<ReLU
predictions.scope: noisy mixed target; a failed prediction retained

statistical_unit: one target recipe and sample-size/noise conditions; four paired data/feature repeats
